title: DStv E16 — No Satellite Signal
likelyCauses: Dish is misaligned (wind, knock, or installation drift)
Damaged/loose coaxial cable or connector (F-connector corrosion)
steps: Check the weather — if it's raining heavily, wait 15-20 minutes; this is often temporary rain fade.
Inspect the dish for physical movement, obstruction (tree branches, new structure) or damage.
Check all F-connectors at the LNB and at the decoder for corrosion or looseness; re-seat/tighten them.
Run the decoder's signal strength/quality test (Settings > Dish Alignment / Signal Test).
If signal is 0 or very low, re-align the dish in small steps while watching the signal meter.
If signal is unstable only on specific transponders, suspect LNB fault — swap/replace the LNB.
Confirm the dish is still pointed at the correct satellite (position can shift after storms).
partsOrToolsNeeded: Coax crimping tool and new F-connectors
whenToEscalate: If realignment doesn't restore signal and LNB swap doesn't help, check for line-of-sight obstruction or escalate to a dish-mounting/structural issue.
safetyNotes: Never climb onto a roof or mast in wet/windy weather. Use proper fall protection when working at height.

title: DStv E30 — Subscription / Decoder Authorisation Issue
likelyCauses: Subscription expired or payment not yet reflected
Smart card not properly paired/activated with the decoder
Decoder hasn't connected to receive the latest entitlement update
steps: Confirm the account is paid up to date with the customer or via the self-service app/USSD.
Leave the decoder powered on and connected to satellite/internet for at least 30-60 minutes to receive an update.
Try a manual 'Reset Decoder' / 'Request Entitlement' option from the decoder menu if available.
Power-cycle the decoder (unplug 30 seconds, plug back in).
If the smart card was recently swapped, confirm it is pushed in fully and the correct way round.
whenToEscalate: If payment is confirmed but the error persists after 2+ hours, escalate to the pay-TV provider's call centre to manually refresh the smart card.

title: DStv E48 — Smart Card Error
likelyCauses: Smart card inserted incorrectly or dirty contacts
steps: Power off the decoder, remove the smart card, and inspect the gold contacts for dirt/scratches.
Gently clean the contacts with a dry, lint-free cloth (no liquids).
Re-insert the card the correct way (chip facing the correct direction per decoder label) and push fully in.
Power the decoder back on and wait for it to read the card.
If still failing, try the card in another decoder of the same type to isolate card vs reader fault.
whenToEscalate: If the card fails in a known-good decoder too, request a smart card replacement from the provider.

title: GOtv E60/E16 — No or Weak Terrestrial Signal
likelyCauses: Too far from transmission tower / obstruction
steps: Check the aerial cable connections at both the aerial and the decoder.
Inspect the aerial for physical damage or that it hasn't rotated out of position.
Run the decoder's signal strength test and note which channels/frequencies are weak.
Re-aim the aerial toward the known transmitter direction for the area in small increments.
If using a signal booster, check its power supply and that it is not overloading the signal.
Re-scan channels after any aerial adjustment.
whenToEscalate: If no signal is achievable even with a known-good aerial in a good location, the area may be outside coverage — advise customer accordingly.
safetyNotes: Use fall protection when adjusting roof-mounted aerials.

title: StarTimes — No / Weak Signal
steps: Identify whether the StarTimes decoder is the satellite (dish) or digital terrestrial (aerial) variant.
Check and re-seat all cable connections at the decoder and antenna/dish end.
Open Menu > Signal Test and check the signal strength/quality bars.
For satellite: re-align the dish slightly while monitoring the signal meter.
For terrestrial: re-aim the aerial toward the nearest transmitter and re-scan.
Power-cycle the decoder after any adjustment.
whenToEscalate: Escalate to StarTimes support if a hardware swap (LNB/aerial) does not restore signal.
safetyNotes: Avoid working at height in wet or windy conditions.

title: Generic — Subscription/Access Denied Message
steps: Verify payment status with the customer/provider app.
Ensure decoder has clear signal and is left on to receive entitlement updates for 30-60 minutes.
Power-cycle the decoder.
Check if a cheaper package was selected that excludes the scrambled channel.
whenToEscalate: Contact the provider's call centre if payment is confirmed but access is still denied after a few hours.

title: TV — No Power / Won't Turn On
likelyCauses: Blown internal fuse / failed power supply board
steps: Confirm the wall socket works with another device (phone charger, lamp).
Check the power cable is firmly seated at both the TV and the socket; try a different cable if available.
Unplug the TV for 60 seconds (power drain), then plug back in and try powering on.
Check for a blinking standby LED pattern — count the blinks, this often indicates a specific fault code (refer to the TV brand's manual).
If completely dead with no LED at all, the internal power supply board or fuse has likely failed and needs a qualified repair technician.
whenToEscalate: No LED activity at all after confirming mains power is good → escalate to board-level repair or replacement.
safetyNotes: Always unplug the TV before opening the back panel. Capacitors can hold a charge after power-off — do not open the chassis unless trained.

title: TV — No Picture but Sound Works
likelyCauses: Faulty main board or T-con board
steps: Shine a torch close to the screen at an angle — if you can faintly see a picture, the backlight has failed (panel/board issue).
Confirm the correct HDMI/AV input source is selected.
Try a different HDMI cable and a different source device to rule out the cable/source.
If backlight is confirmed failed, this needs a panel/board level repair — not user-serviceable.
whenToEscalate: Backlight or T-con board failure requires a TV repair technician with the correct replacement parts.
safetyNotes: Do not open the TV panel — high voltage components inside even when unplugged (capacitor discharge risk).

title: Remote Control Not Responding
likelyCauses: IR sensor on TV/decoder blocked or dirty
steps: Replace the batteries with fresh ones, checking correct polarity.
Clean the IR emitter (front of remote) and the IR receiver window on the TV/decoder.
Test the remote using a phone camera — point the remote at the camera and press a button; a working IR remote will show a flickering purple/white light on screen.
If no light shows, the remote's IR LED has likely failed — try a replacement remote.
For RF/Bluetooth remotes, re-pair following the decoder/TV's pairing procedure.
Remove any obstruction between remote and the device's sensor.
whenToEscalate: If a known-good replacement remote also fails to control the device, the IR/RF receiver inside the TV/decoder may be faulty.

title: 'No Signal' on TV with Decoder/Source Connected via HDMI
steps: Confirm the TV is set to the correct HDMI input number matching the cable used.
Check the decoder/source device is powered on (not just the TV).
Re-seat the HDMI cable at both ends; try a different cable.
Try the same cable/source on a different HDMI port on the TV to isolate a faulty port.
Power-cycle both the TV and the source device.
whenToEscalate: If the source works on another TV's HDMI port but not on this TV's ports, the TV's HDMI board needs repair.

title: Smart TV with Built-in Tuner — No Channels Found (No External Decoder)
likelyCauses: Aerial/antenna not connected or connected to the wrong RF/ANT input
Auto channel scan not yet run, or run with the wrong region/country setting
Weak or no terrestrial signal in the area
TV set to the wrong source (should be 'TV'/'Antenna', not HDMI) for built-in tuner channels
steps: Confirm there is no set-top box/decoder — the TV's own built-in tuner is being used directly.
Check the aerial/antenna cable is firmly connected to the TV's RF/ANT-IN port (not a decoder, since there isn't one).
On the TV, select the correct input/source: 'TV' or 'Antenna' (not HDMI/AV).
Go to Settings > Channel/Broadcast setup > Auto Tune (wording varies by brand) and run a full channel scan, confirming the correct country/region.
If zero or very few channels are found, check signal strength in the TV's tuner menu and consider repositioning/replacing the aerial.

For areas with only satellite coverage, note that most smart TVs need an external satellite decoder — a built-in tuner alone usually only receives free-to-air terrestrial (DVB-T2) channels, not satellite.
whenToEscalate: If signal is confirmed present at the aerial but the TV still finds no channels after a rescan, the TV's internal tuner may be faulty — escalate for repair.
safetyNotes: Use fall protection when adjusting roof-mounted aerials.

title: Smart TV — Streaming Apps / Wi-Fi / Casting Not Working (No Decoder Involved)
likelyCauses: TV not connected to Wi-Fi, or weak/unstable Wi-Fi signal
App needs an update or has a temporary server-side outage
TV's smart platform software is outdated
Router/network issue (DNS, internet down) rather than the TV itself
steps: Confirm the issue is with the TV's own smart platform/apps, not an external decoder (no decoder is involved in this fault).
Check Settings > Network on the TV — confirm it shows 'Connected' with a good signal strength; reconnect to Wi-Fi if needed.
Test another device (phone) on the same Wi-Fi to rule out a broader internet/router problem.
Restart the TV (unplug 30 seconds) and the router/modem.
Update the specific app (e.g., Netflix, YouTube) via the TV's app store, and check for a pending TV system/software update.
If only one app fails across multiple networks, suspect a server-side outage with that streaming service.
For casting/screen mirroring, ensure both the TV and the mobile device are on the same Wi-Fi network.
whenToEscalate: If Wi-Fi connects fine but all apps fail and a software update doesn't help, the TV's smart platform/firmware may need a factory reset or technician-level reflash.

title: Decoder Stuck on Boot Logo / Restart Loop
steps: Unplug the decoder from power for a full 2 minutes, then plug back in.
If it has a reset button/pinhole, perform a factory reset per the manual (note: this may erase recordings).
Check the power is stable (not from an overloaded extension strip); plug directly into a wall socket.
If the decoder has a hard drive (PVR), listen for unusual clicking sounds, indicating drive failure.
If reset does not resolve it, the decoder likely needs a technician-level software re-flash or unit swap.
whenToEscalate: Escalate to provider's technical support/unit swap if factory reset does not resolve the loop.
